item.title: Phrasal verbs for work 与 “工作” 相关的短语动词
item.description:
节目简介

在职场中为了获得更好的发展，我们可能需要 “put in time and effort（付出时间和努力）”，积极地 “take on new challenges（接受新的挑战）”，并且不断 “come up with ideas（提出新的想法）”。看视频，跟主持人 Georgie 学习七个和 “工作” 相关的短语动词。

用法总结

  • take (something) on 接受（工作）；承担（责任）

She decided to take on a new project at work, even though she was already busy.

  • come up with (something) 想出，提出（想法）

She came up with a brilliant marketing strategy that boosted sales.

  • put in (something) 付出…；投入…

He's been putting in a lot of effort to improve his performance at work.

  • knuckle down 开始努力工作或学习

Let's get rid of all the distractions and knuckle down so I can get this project done.

  • get ahead 领先；提前

She worked hard to get ahead in her career and eventually became a manager.

  • look into (something) 调查，研究（某事）

The HR department is looking into the complaints made by the employees.

  • get back to (someone) 给（某人）回话

I'll get back to you with more information after I discuss it with the team.

item.title: Phrasal verbs for climate change 与 “气候变化” 相关的短语动词
item.description:
节目简介

“Climate change（气候变化）” 给地球环境带来的影响日益严重......你知道如何用英语来谈论与 “气候变化” 和 “环境保护” 相关的话题吗？从大气层 “heat up（升温）” 到水源 “dry up（干涸）” ，从在日常生活中 “cut down on（减少）” 碳排放的行为，到 “take part in（参与）” 更多减少浪费的行动……本期视频中，主持人 Georgie 将介绍八个与 “气候变化” 有关的短语动词。

用法总结

  • heat up 使…...变暖，升温

The planet is heating up due to a high level of CO2 in the atmosphere.

  • rely on 依靠，依赖

Humans rely on fossil fuels to heat our homes and fuel our cars.

  • dry up 干涸

This valley used to be a lake but it dried up centuries ago.

  • die out 消亡

Some traditional skills are dying out in modern society.

  • wipe out 使…...彻底消失，使…...灭绝

Pollution and deforestation have wiped out entire ecosystems.

  • cut down on 减少

One way to combat climate change is to cut down on our use of fossil fuels.

  • fight for 努力争取

The community is fighting for cleaner air and water in their neighbourhood.

  • push for 反复推动，倡导

The workers are pushing for higher wages and better conditions.

  • take part in 参与

I took part in a beach clean-up event and together we removed 200 bags of rubbish.

item.title: Phrasal verbs for eating 与 “吃” 相关的短语动词
item.description:
节目简介

无论是解馋的小零食，还是令人大快朵颐的主菜，美食的魅力总是让人难以抗拒。你知道 “吃零食”、“大快朵颐” 以及 “在外吃饭” 分别怎么说吗？在本期节目中，主持人 Georgie 分享七个与 “吃” 相关的短语动词。

用法总结

  • snack on (something) 吃（某种）零食

She likes to snack on almonds while she works.

  • munch on (something) 吃，大声咀嚼（某食物）

They munched on popcorn at the cinema.

  • dig in (to something) 开吃，痛快地吃

The food looks delicious — let's dig in!

  • tuck in (to something) 开吃，痛快地吃

The children tucked into their pancakes with delight.

  • eat (something) up 吃光，吃完

You'd better eat up all your vegetables before you leave the table!

  • pig out 大吃大喝，狼吞虎咽

We usually pig out on snacks when we have movie nights.

  • eat out 在饭馆用餐，在外用餐

I love eating out, but it can be expensive if you do it all the time.

item.title: Phrasal verbs for sleep 与 “睡眠” 相关的短语动词
item.description:
节目简介

一夜好眠，满满能量！ 睡眠（sleep）不仅是身体的修复时间，更是思绪的放松时刻。你知道 “nod off”、“doze off” 以及 “crash out” 在英语中分别是什么意思吗？在本期节目中，主次人 Georgie 将详细讲解七个与 “睡眠” 有关的短语动词。

用法总结

  • lie down 躺下

He lay down on the sofa to watch some TV and ended up falling asleep.

  • stay up 熬夜，深夜不睡觉

We stayed up late watching movies until 2am.

  • doze off 或 nod off 打盹儿，打瞌睡

He dozed off during the lecture because he was so tired.

It doesn't matter how interested Dad is in the film, he always nods off.

  • crash out （因疲劳而）很快入睡

After the long hike, everyone crashed out as soon as they got back to the cabin.

  • sleep through 不被（噪声等）吵醒

She slept through her alarm and was consequently late for work.

  • sleep on (something) 推迟对（某事）作出决定

Before making any decisions, it's always good to sleep on it and think it over.

item.title: Phrasal verbs for feelings 与 “情绪和感受” 相关的短语动词
item.description:
节目简介

你遇到过 “break down” 情绪崩溃的时刻吗？当有负面情绪的时候，你会选择 “open up” 敞开心扉、和别人沟通交流？还是会 “bottle up your feelings” 压抑、掩饰你的情绪？在本期节目中，主持人 Georgie 将讲解七个在谈论与 “情绪和感受” 相关的话题时可以用到的短语动词。一起来学习吧！

用法总结

  • bottle up 抑制、掩饰（情绪）

He tends to bottle up his anger, which often leads to stress.

  • open up 敞开心扉，吐露心声

After years of keeping everything inside, she finally opened up to her therapist.

  • hold (something) back 忍住，不表露

He wanted to tell her the truth, but he decided to hold back.

  • break down （情绪）崩溃

After weeks of stress, he finally broke down and cried.

  • blow up （情绪）失控，暴怒

He blew up at his work colleague for making the same mistake again.

  • freak out 使（情绪）极度激动

Don't freak out, but there's a spider on your shoulder!

  • calm down 冷静下来

After taking a few deep breaths, I started to calm down.

  • chill out 放松，冷静

They spent the weekend chilling out by the beach, forgetting about their worries.

item.title: Phrasal verbs for travel 与 “旅行” 相关的短语动词
item.description:
节目简介

你上一次出门旅行是什么时候？会不会等不及开启 “set off” 下一场说走就走的旅行呢？在本期节目中，主持人 Georgie 将分享七个与 “旅行” 有关的短语动词，一起来学习吧！

用法总结

  • look forward to (something) 期盼，期望（某事）

He's really looking forward to his summer holiday by the beach.

  • get away 外出度假

I'm feeling burnt out. I'd love to get away for a few days and spend time in the countryside.

  • pick (someone) up 接（某人）

The taxi picked the woman up from her house and took her to the airport.

  • hurry up 快点

Hurry up! We're going to miss our flight!

  • set off 启程、出发

Grandpa set off at 6am to make sure he arrived at the airport early for his flight.

  • check in 办理登机手续，办理入住手续

After checking in at the hotel reception, she gave them the room key.

  • take off 起飞

The plane took off smoothly and then we were in the air.

item.title: Phrasal verbs for technology 与 “技术” 相关的短语动词
item.description:
节目简介

你知道 “log in” 和 “sign up” 有什么区别吗？“Turn up”、“turn down” 以及 “switch on”、“turn off” 怎么使用更地道？在本期节目中，主持人 Georgie 将详细讲解与技术 “technology” 有关的 12 个短语动词，一起来学习吧！

本期内容

  • log in 或 sign in 登录

I can't log in because I'm struggling to remember my password!

Please sign in with your username and password to access your account.

  • log out 或 sign out 退出

Remember to log out of your online banking after use so no one else can access your details.

If you're done using the app, make sure to sign out to protect your privacy.

  • sign up 注册

If you want to be the first to hear about concert tickets, sign up to the mailing list.

  • scroll through 滚动浏览

I want to read more books, but first I need to break the habit of scrolling through social media whenever I'm bored.

  • turn on 或 switch on 打开

I was bored, so I turned the TV on and started watching.

It is freezing today! Can you please turn on the heater?

  • turn off 或 switch off 关闭、关掉

Remember to turn off your computer before you leave the office.

Remember to switch off the lights when you leave a room to save energy.

  • turn up 调大、增强

I can't hear the TV - can you turn it up?

  • turn down 调小、减弱

The party next door is so noisy. Shall we ask them to turn the music down?

  • set up 创建，设置

My grandparents have finally got wi-fi, but I need to help them set it up.

item.title: Phrasal verbs for health and fitness 与 “健康和健身” 相关的短语动词
item.description:
节目简介

如今，人们越来越重视运动 “work out” 给身体带来的诸多好处。从坚持 “stick to” 健身计划到科学热身 “warm up”、冷身 “cool down”，本期视频，主持人 Georgie 分享了七个与 “健康和健身” 有关的实用短语动词。

用法总结

  • warm up 热身

Let's warm up before the race by doing a light jog around the field.

  • work out 锻炼身体

I try to work out at least twice a week. It helps to relieve stress.

  • cool down 冷身

After running, I cool down by walking for five minutes, then stretching.

 

  • stick to 坚持

I'm really proud of my daughter for sticking to her football training programme.

  • give up 放弃

After six attempts at jumping two metres and failing, she gave up.

  • cut down (on) 减少，削减

I really need to cut down on sugary snacks after meals if I want to feel healthier.

  • cut out 完全去除，戒除

Lifting weights was giving me neck pain, so I've cut that out of my workout routine.

item.title: Phrasal verbs for money 与 “金钱” 相关的短语动词
item.description:
节目简介

金钱 “money” 是日常生活中避免不了的主题，那么，用英语该怎么地道、自然地谈论这个话题呢？英语中的 “save up”、“live on” 和 “get by” 分别都是什么意思？在本期节目中，主持人 Georgie 介绍了七个与 “金钱” 相关的高频短语动词。

用法总结

  • fork out （尤指不情愿地）付钱

I had to fork out a lot of money to repair my car after the accident.

  • splash out 花大笔的钱，挥霍

She decided to splash out on a luxury handbag for her birthday.

  • pay (someone) back 还（某人）钱

My dream is to pay my parents back for all the money they spent on my education.

  • run out of (money) （钱）用光了

Unfortunately, we ran out of money before we finished building the shed, and we couldn't pay for more materials.

  • live on 靠……生活

Since retiring, my grandparents are able to live on their state pensions.

  • get by 勉强过活

I get by with my salary, but I don't have enough to save up or treat myself to luxuries.

  • save up 存钱

My sister is saving up to buy a house.

item.title: Phrasal verbs for education 与 “教育” 相关的短语动词
item.description:
节目简介

如果你对一件事情很感兴趣 “be into something”，你可能想参加与之相关的培训课程 “take up a course”，或者自己阅读、研究 “read up on” 相关资料。在本期节目，主持人 Georgie 将分享八个与 “教育” 密切相关的短语动词。

本期内容

  • be into (something) 非常喜欢，热衷于（某事）

Many teenagers nowadays are into gaming and spend hours playing with friends.

  • take (something) up 开始参与（某工作或活动）

During retirement, Mr Johnson took up gardening to stay active and spend time outdoors.

  • read up on (something) 广泛阅读，研究（某领域）

Before starting his business, Jack spent weeks reading up on entrepreneurship.

  • brush up on (something) 温习，复习（某项技能）

Mark did a refresher course to brush up on his accounting skills before starting his new job.

  • work on (something) 改进，下功夫做（某事）

She needs to work on her time management so she can meet deadlines more easily.

  • fall behind 落后

Because of her illness, Sarah fell behind in her coursework.

  • catch up (on something) 追赶（某事的）进度

Once Sarah recovered from her illness, she took some time to catch up on her coursework.

  • hand (something) in 提交，上交（某物）

Once Sarah had caught up on her coursework, she handed it in to her teacher.

item.title: Phrasal verbs for friendship 与 “友谊” 相关的短语动词
item.description:
节目简介

从建立友谊到解决冲突，下面这些实用的短语动词可以帮助我们在用英语谈论 “友谊” 时更加自然地表达。你知道 “和……相处愉快”、“和……闹翻” 以及 “和……和好” 用英语怎么说吗？在本期节目中，主持人 Georgie 将分享七个与 “友谊” 相关的短语动词。

用法总结

  • get on (with someone) 与（某人）相处融洽

My sister and I really get on. We have a lot of fun together!

  • fall out (with someone) 与（某人）闹翻

Mia and Nathan fell out after Mia lied and didn’t apologise.

  • run into (someone) 撞见（某人）

Two childhood friends ran into each other in a London coffee shop.

  • hear from (someone) 收到（某人的）消息

I was thrilled to hear from my long-lost friend after years of being out of touch.

  • make up (with someone) 与（某人）和好

It took time, but eventually the siblings made up and repaired their relationship.

  • hang out (with someone) 与（某人）共度时光

At the weekend, my friends and I hang out at the local coffee shop.

  • catch up (with someone) 与（某人）交流近况

Family reunions are great opportunities to catch up with relatives you don’t see often.
